## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Generate a generic distribution in log10 readout space
plot_data <- data.frame(
  log_readout = seq(0, 6, length.out = 1500)
) %>%
  mutate(
    cell_count = dnorm(log_readout, mean = 3, sd = 0.8) * 1800
  )

# Sorting boundaries: bottom 5%, bottom 10%, top 10%, and top 5%
bin_boundaries <- qnorm(
  c(0.02, 0.11, 0.89, 0.98),
  mean = 3,
  sd = 0.8
)

plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    bin = case_when(
      log_readout <= bin_boundaries[1] ~ "Bin 1",
      log_readout <= bin_boundaries[2] ~ "Bin 2",
      log_readout >= bin_boundaries[4] ~ "Bin 3",
      log_readout >= bin_boundaries[3] ~ "Bin 4",
      TRUE ~ "Not sorted"
    ),
    bin = factor(
      bin,
      levels = c(
    "Bin 1",
    "Bin 2",
        "Not sorted",
    "Bin 3",
    "Bin 4"
      )
    )
  )

# Positions for bin labels
bin_label_positions <- data.frame(
  label = c(
    "Bin 1",
    "Bin 2",
    "Bin 3",
    "Bin 4"
  ),
  log_readout = c(
    mean(c(0, bin_boundaries[1])),
    mean(bin_boundaries[1:2]),
    mean(bin_boundaries[3:4]),
    mean(c(bin_boundaries[4], 6))
  ),
  cell_count = max(plot_data$cell_count) * 0.62
)

cell_sorting_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = log_readout, y = cell_count)
) +
  geom_area(aes(fill = bin), alpha = 0.65) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.4, colour = "#527FB8") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = bin_boundaries,
    linewidth = 1.1,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = bin_label_positions,
    aes(
      x = log_readout,
      y = cell_count,
      label = label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Bin 1" = "#4C78A8",
      "Bin 2" = "#9EC1DE",
      "Not sorted" = "#DCE6F0",
      "Bin 3" = "#F4A582",
      "Bin 4" = "#C94C4C"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 0:6,
    labels = c(
      "0",
      expression(10^1),
      expression(10^2),
      expression(10^3),
      expression(10^4),
      expression(10^5),
      expression(10^6)
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, max(plot_data$cell_count) * 1.08),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Cell Sorting",
    x = "Readout",
    y = "Cell count"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 22,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = 15)
    ),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.8),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

cell_sorting_plot

ggsave(
  "/g/steinmetz/link/cell_sorting_four_bins.png",
  cell_sorting_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 5.5,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
